title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.0.1-rc.11
summary: Make the settings divider visible and correct stale row heights that can leave empty scrolling space.
changes: Use a solid grey separator above keyboard shortcuts instead of a two-pixel 3D border.
Apply each row’s current width before measuring its wrapped height, and position subsequent rows from the actual resulting bounds.
Add rendered-pixel checks and real-settings-form layout coverage at scaled geometry/text sizes, after tab switches and narrow/wide window transitions. Record a CI rendering for visual inspection.
Preserve RC10’s multiline mapping editor, clearer help, saved preferences, and compact settings layout.
testing: Open Other Options and confirm a visible grey line separates keyboard shortcuts from the options above.
Switch among all settings tabs several times. Other Options should fit at the usual size without a scrollbar through empty space.
Check at your normal Windows display scaling; if a genuinely small window requires scrolling, it should stop at the final setting.
Confirm the IP Mappings box still shows multiple lines and your saved preferences remain intact.
known_limitations: Real Windows Explorer, physical display scaling, startup/uninstall, and two-PC behavior still need the manual checks above; automated tests cannot replace them.

Receiving-folder and automatic-close preferences belong to each PC. Changing the folder affects new durable drag/drop transfers only; existing jobs and legacy clipboard file copying keep their prior destinations.

The receiving folder must be an accessible ordinary local directory. Linked directories and unavailable drives are rejected. No overwrite/merge, protocol, concurrency, speed, service, or automatic-update behavior is added.
Use the same RC on both PCs for consistent Settings. RC6/RC7 protocol-2 transfers remain compatible; older EXEs may discard the new preference fields if they rewrite the same preferences file.
Full-speed Wi-Fi transfers can still cause mouse lag. Offline temporary data can only be cleaned when the peer reconnects.
